In 2024, 92.5% of new power generation came from renewables. At the same time, AI is reshaping how we design, manage, and use energy, from smart grids to predictive maintenance. But these are not isolated shifts - they are twin engines of a new development era.

The renewable energy sector already supports 16.2 million jobs. By 2050, it could generate another 40 million. AI is also creating new roles - but it’s also consuming vast resources. In 2024, AI used more electricity than 150 countries individually, with projections set to double within a few years. That same energy could have powered basic access for ~1 billion people.

However the risks are not just environmental. Automation threatens jobs. Unequal access to energy, data, and digital skills threatens inclusion. 61% of people believe AI will support their work, yet many in low and medium HDI countries still lack the tools to participate in this future.

How do we build a just transition, not just a fast one?

1️⃣ Shift from extraction to local value creation: Build domestic supply chains for minerals, manufacturing, and services.

2️⃣ Close the digital divide: Expand digital and energy infrastructure so that everyone can access the future of work.

3️⃣ Align finance with inclusive transitions: Invest in national institutions, technical skills, and utility reform to empower countries to lead their own energy-AI pathways.

As we look to the G20, COP30, and the UN Financing for Development Summit, the imperative is clear: the energy transition must be smart, fast and fair. To find out more, I invite you to read this previous edition of the Sustainable Energy Bulletin: 👉 https://lnkd.in/eY_FBqgp
